UPDATE WISH FILE based on council review, then run /review on the updated wish.

## Wish to update: .genie/wishes/sdk-compliance-tests/WISH.md

## Council Verdict: MODIFY — Reduce to ~20% of original scope

The council (0 APPROVE, 2 MODIFY, 4 REJECT) found the original 7-group plan is overengineered because:
- All 4 channels are already consistent (4/4 on every dimension)
- Runtime validator already exists at packages/channel-sdk/src/discovery/validator.ts
- Source-level grep tests are fragile and weak signals
- All 3 blockers (#81, #85, #86) still open

### NEW SCOPE:

**Focus on the ONE thing not caught by TypeScript or the runtime validator:**
Capability-method consistency — "if you declare canStreamResponse=true, you must implement createStreamSender()"

**Execution groups (2, not 7):**
1. **Enhance existing validator.ts** — add capability-method pairing validation to validatePluginInterface(). If canStreamResponse=true, check createStreamSender exists. If canFetchHistory=true, check fetchHistory exists. Etc. This gives RUNTIME enforcement, not just test-time.
2. **Parameterized test** — single test file that loads all 6 channel plugins (add a2a + internal to scope) and runs validatePluginInterface() on each. Plus capability-method consistency assertions.

**DROP from scope:**
- Groups 4-5 (source-level grep for utility usage and journey timing)
- Group 6 (todo stubs for open blockers)
- Most of Groups 2-3 (structural tests that duplicate validator.ts)

**Key files:**
- packages/channel-sdk/src/discovery/validator.ts (enhance)
- packages/channel-sdk/src/__tests__/compliance.test.ts (new, slim)

Update the WISH.md with this reduced scope. Then run /review on it.

You are DONE when the wish is updated AND the review verdict is delivered.
